title: even when use_external_editor is set to true and exec_path / exec_flags are correctly configured.
body:
### Tested versions

4.6.stable.mono (official)

### System information

Windows 11, VS Code 1.124.2 (x64), .NET / C# project

### Issue description

When Script Editor is unchecked in Manage Editor Features (the toolbar toggle dropdown), Godot silently ignores all script-click interactions — including launching the configured external editor — even when use_external_editor is set to true and exec_path / exec_flags are correctly configured.

Expected behavior:
Unchecking Script Editor should only hide/disable the built-in script editor panel. The external editor (configured in Editor Settings → Text Editor → External) should still be launched when clicking a script, since the user has explicitly opted into using an external tool.

Actual behavior:
Clicking any script resource in the FileSystem dock or Scene tree does nothing. No error, no toast, no VS Code window — the click is silently dropped.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open any Godot 4.6 project (C# or GDScript).
2. Go to Editor → Editor Settings → Text Editor → External:
✅ Use External Editor
Exec Path: path to Code.exe (or any valid editor)
Exec Flags: --goto {file}:{line}:{col}
3. Confirm external editor works by clicking a script → VS Code opens.
4. In the toolbar, click the Manage Editor Features dropdown and uncheck Script Editor.
5. Click any script again → nothing happens.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Why this is confusing
Setting | User expects | Actually happens
-- | -- | --
Script Editor unchecked | Built-in editor hidden; external editor still works | ALL script interactions silently ignored
Use External Editor ✅ | External editor always invoked | Only when Script Editor is also checked

The Script Editor toggle functions as a global gatekeeper for all script interactions, not just the built-in panel. But the name Script Editor is read by most users as "the built-in script editor panel", making it natural to turn off when using an external editor — which then breaks the very thing they're trying to use.

Workaround
Keep Script Editor checked in Manage Editor Features, even when using an external editor.

Minimal reproduction project
Any project with a script file attached to a node. No custom code needed.
